entries.name: Rook
entries.migrates: partial migration; flocks wander far in winter
behaviour: nests in vast noisy treetop colonies called rookeries
probes loose soil with a decurved bill for worms and grubs
the sound of a ploughed field in spring

voxel_model.pattern: glossy black with bare grey bill base

entries.notes: The agricultural crow of the Eurasian black-earth steppe; model rookeries as distant noise and moving black clouds over ploughed fields. gestation_days is incubation.

entries.name: Eurasian magpie
behaviour: tail is half the body length and flashes white in flight
domed stick nest with a roof of thorns
infamous (and exaggerated) hoarder of bright objects

voxel_model.pattern: pied black-and-white with steely blue-green tail

entries.notes: A clever corvid common at field edges and farmsteads; one of the most recognisable silhouettes on open ground. gestation_days is incubation.

entries.name: Common quail
entries.migrates: long-distance migration to Africa and India for winter
behaviour: crex-crex whistle heard at night in summer fields
reluctant to flush; runs then rises steeply
farmland favourite; numbers collapse with converted grassland

voxel_model.pattern: streaked buff with pale throat and eyebrow

entries.notes: A ground-hugging gamebird invisible until it bursts from the grass at the last second; classic flushing quarry. gestation_days is incubation.

entries.name: Eurasian hoopoe
entries.migrates: migrates to sub-Saharan Africa and South Asia for winter
behaviour: fan-like crest erects in alarm or courtship
slender decurved bill probes dung heaps and soft soil
nest in holes smells of foul secretion; females brood, males feed

voxel_model.pattern: orange with black-and-white barred wings and crest

entries.notes: The most surreal common bird of the dry open country: a salmon arc of wings with a zebra-striped tail, working the dung piles. gestation_days is incubation.

entries.name: European bee-eater
entries.migrates: migrates to sub-Saharan Africa for winter
behaviour: sallies from a perch to snatch flying insects, clears stings on a branch
nests in burrows excavated in sandy banks and cliffs
rainbow of turquoise, chestnut and yellow in breeding plumage

voxel_model.pattern: rainbow bands of turquoise, chestnut and yellow

entries.notes: Colonies burrow into sandy steppe banks; the birds hawk bees above the colony. gestation_days is incubation.

entries.name: Little owl
behaviour: bobs and bows its flat-crowned head in daytime perches
nests in wall holes, ruins, hollow trees and cliff ledges
big yellow eyes and fierce glaring stare

voxel_model.pattern: brown mottled with white spots and brow ridges

entries.notes: The farmyard owl of the open country; sits in daylight on posts and roofs and glares. gestation_days is incubation.

entries.name: Short-eared owl
entries.migrates: partial migration; winter communal roosts of hundreds
behaviour: hunts low over rough grass in daylight, unlike most owls
ground-nests in tussocks; one of the few open-country owlets
masquerades as a larger owl flattened against the ground

voxel_model.pattern: buff-barred with dark wing patches and yellow eyes

entries.notes: A daylight-hunting owl of open grassland; the only owl that regularly hunts beside harriers over the steppe. gestation_days is incubation.

entries.name: Steppe kestrel (lesser kestrel)
entries.migrates: long-distance migration to Africa and India for winter
behaviour: hunts insects on the wing and from hover, often in noisy flocks
nests colonially on cliffs, ruins and buildings
white claws unique among falcons; hovers over grasshopper plagues

voxel_model.pattern: rufous back, slate head and wing patches in male

entries.notes: The colonial kestrel of the steppe; thousands roosted over West African locust swarms in satellite studies. gestation_days is incubation.

entries.name: Little bustard
entries.migrates: partial migration; winter flocks gather in loose hundreds
behaviour: males strut with puffed white neck in lekking displays
ground-nests; flushes late and flies with whirring wings
near threatened; a vanishing icon of the European steppe

voxel_model.pattern: grey-brown with white neck ring and barred flanks

entries.notes: The smaller ghost of the great bustard; its lekking boom is a vanishing sound of the open grasslands. gestation_days is incubation.

entries.name: Horned lark
entries.migrates: partial migration; northern populations move south in winter
behaviour: two black feather tufts rise like horns on the head
walks rather than hops; nests scrape into bare ground
glassy, tinkling flight song; the first bird back on spring plows

voxel_model.pattern: sandy above, black horns, yellow face, dark breastband

entries.notes: Also called the shore lark in North America; the most widespread open-country songbird on Earth, tundra to steppe. gestation_days is incubation.

entries.name: Calandra lark
entries.migrates: partial migration to milder winter quarters
behaviour: sings in sustained display flights high above territory
expert mimic weaving other birds into its song
stouter and darker than skylark; walks on the ground

voxel_model.pattern: grey-brown streaked with black breast patches

entries.notes: The classic Mediterranean and steppe lark; its flight song carries across kilometres of open country. gestation_days is incubation.

entries.name: Isabelline wheatear
entries.migrates: migrates to Africa and the Middle East for winter
behaviour: sandy ghost on the ground; nearly invisible until it flushes
nests deep inside ground-squirrel and rodent burrows
upright stance with quick tail-flicks revealing the black tail base

voxel_model.pattern: uniform sandy-buff with black-tipped tail

entries.notes: The beige wheatear that disappears against bare dirt; its reliance on rodent burrows ties it to the burrowing steppe fauna. gestation_days is incubation.

entries.name: Pied wheatear
entries.migrates: migrates to India and Africa for winter
behaviour: male is a living nun: crisp black-and-white head and throat
perches on stones and bushes at road edges and ruins
nests in rocky crevices and stone walls

voxel_model.pattern: pied black and white with sandy mantle

entries.notes: A spectacularly patterned little chat of the stony steppe; the male's hooded monk plumage is unmistakable. gestation_days is incubation.

entries.name: Pallas's sandgrouse
entries.migrates: irruptive; mass westward invasions in seed-failure years
behaviour: feathered feet and bristled nostrils for steppe winds
in some years millions erupt westwards over Europe
streams to water holes at dawn and dusk like black-bellied sandgrouse

voxel_model.pattern: sandy with black belly bar and long pointed tail

entries.notes: The irruptive steppe sandgrouse; 'sandgrouse years' in old European sporting books record birds as far as Britain. gestation_days is incubation.

entries.name: Greater prairie chicken
behaviour: males boom and stamp on 'leks' at dawn, orange air sacs inflated
tail flares in display; dance accompanied by drumming wing-beats
vanished across most of its range as tallgrass prairie went to corn

voxel_model.pattern: barred brown with orange neck sacs and orange eye combs

entries.notes: The booming ghost of the tallgrass prairie; leks are communal stages worth scripting as rare landmark events. gestation_days is incubation.

entries.name: Western meadowlark
behaviour: flute-like bubbling song from fence posts at dawn
bright yellow breast with black V-shaped bib
meadowlark nests are domed and woven into grass

voxel_model.pattern: streaked brown above, yellow below with black V

entries.notes: The song of the North American grassland, unrelated to true larks; its yellow bib and fluting whistle are the prairie's signature. gestation_days is incubation.

entries.name: Burrowing owl
entries.migrates: partial migration in the north of the range
behaviour: nests in abandoned prairie-dog burrows; rarely digs its own
bobs and curtseys at the burrow mouth when alarmed
lines the den with dung; rattles like a rattlesnake when threatened

voxel_model.pattern: sandy-spotted with white brow and long legs

entries.notes: The little owl that lives in prairie-dog towns; model it paired with prairie dog holes as a sign of a healthy grassland colony. gestation_days is incubation.

entries.name: Marbled polecat
behaviour: skunk-like arched display with curled tail and foul secretion
takes over great gerbil and ground-squirrel burrows
weak eyesight; hunts by smell in morning and evening

voxel_model.pattern: yellow mottled with dark spots, black mask, white mouth

entries.notes: Vulnerable across its range and threatened by rodenticides; the masked phantom of the great gerbil warrens. gestation includes long delayed implantation (243-327 days).

entries.name: Least weasel
behaviour: smallest carnivore on Earth; turns white in snowy parts of its range
squeezes through gaps the width of two fingers to follow voles
relentless hunter; surplus kiling caches extra voles in grassy larders

voxel_model.pattern: chestnut above, white below, dark tail tip

entries.notes: The mouse-sized weasel that can follow a vole straight into its burrow; a genuinely pocket-sized predator for the voxel scale.

entries.name: Daurian hedgehog
behaviour: rolls into a tight spine-ball when threatened
hibernates deeply in burrows and rock crevices
forages along roads at night; a common roadkill casualty

voxel_model.pattern: banded spines of white and brown

entries.notes: The hedgehog of the Mongolian steppe; common along field roads and At night foraging the margins.

entries.name: European souslik
behaviour: hibernates 6 to 9 months of the year in plugged burrows
upright sentries whistle on mounds over the colony
declined across Europe as steppe was ploughed; now rare

voxel_model.pattern: grey-brown with pale flank wash and short tail

entries.notes: The souslik of the Central European dry grasslands; its vanishing whistles mark lost steppe habitat.

entries.name: Great gerbil
behaviour: forms huge family-owning burrow complexes with mounds and spoil heaps
a historic reservoir of plague in Central Asia
harvests saltwort stems and stores them in underground larders

voxel_model.pattern: sandy-buff with creamy belly and tufted tail

entries.notes: The great engine of the Central Asian steppe ecology; its burrow colonies drive plague cycles and fascinate Soviet-era literature.

entries.name: Steppe lemming
behaviour: populations cycle every few years, then crash
builds grassy nests under tufts rather than burrowing deeply
grey woolly coat with a mouse-like short tail

voxel_model.pattern: smoky grey above, white below, stubby black tail

entries.notes: The lemming of the Eurasian steppe; its boom-and-bust years feed every small predator on the grassland.

entries.name: Brandt's vole
behaviour: piles neat mounds of cut grass 'haystacks' above its burrow
a serious forage pest in Mongolian herding country
moves in dense family colonies through the summer

voxel_model.pattern: grey-brown above, pale belly, short tail

entries.notes: The haystack rodent of the Mongolian steppe; overgrazed pasture turns to vole towns almost overnight.

entries.name: Striped dwarf hamster
behaviour: cheek pouches haul seed to underground granaries
the small grey hamster of the Baraba steppe
shallow burrows with separate sleeping and larder chambers

voxel_model.pattern: grey-brown with dark dorsal stripe

entries.notes: The Baraba steppe hamster; a granivore small enough to vanish under a single hoofprint.

entries.name: Roborovski's dwarf hamster
behaviour: fastest and smallest of the dwarf hamsters; ricochets across dunes
sand-dweller of semi-desert margins
famous in the pet trade; wild ancestors run in small family groups

voxel_model.pattern: sandy gold with white brow spots and white belly

entries.notes: The tiny desert racer of the Gobi margins; about the size of a walnut, and twice as quick.

entries.name: Plains vizcacha
behaviour: packs burrow entrances with sticks, stones and stolen tools
colonies with decades of tunnelling beneath the pampa
males guard the colony; females form stable groups

voxel_model.pattern: grey-brown with pale belly and stiff white whiskers

entries.notes: The bushy-tailed pampa chinchilla; ranchers curse its hoarding of saddles, brooms and fence posts into its stick piles.

entries.name: Pampas fox
behaviour: thin dog-like fox with a black-tipped bushy tail marked with a pale band
raids poultry and lambing pens around estancias
adjusts instantly to farmland mosaic of the pampas

voxel_model.pattern: sandy-grey with pale muzzle and black tail tip

entries.notes: The pampas shepherd's eternal enemy; a lean generalist that thrives at the cattle-grass edge.

entries.name: Toad-headed agama
behaviour: frog-snouted head and earless sides are a sand-camouflage masterpiece
flattens against dunes or buries itself in seconds
gapes a black-and-white mouth at predators to look bigger

voxel_model.pattern: sandy mottled with dark spots, black-red tail underside

entries.notes: The little frog-faced lizard of the dunes; half the steppe lizards a player sees are toad-headed agamas perfectly matching bare sand.

entries.name: Sand lizard
behaviour: males blaze emerald and green in spring before fading to brown
sunbathes on warm slopes and vanish into grass when approached
common across Europe east to Central Asia on dry slopes

voxel_model.pattern: green flanks with dark eyebrow stripe in males

entries.notes: The emerald-backed lizard of dry European slopes; gestation_days is incubation.

entries.name: Mongolian sand boa
behaviour: swims through loose sand like a fish
blunt shovel-snout and upturned eyes adapted for burial hunting
gives birth to live young rather than laying eggs

voxel_model.pattern: sandy blotches over pale yellow body

entries.notes: A sand-swimming constrictor of the dunes; it hunts by feeling footsteps through grains. gestation_days is the live-birth carry; length is the longest females.

entries.name: Daurian toad
behaviour: breeds explosively in spring ponds and temporary pools
hibernates deep underground through the freezing winter
walks rather than hops; warty skin drips with mild toxins

voxel_model.pattern: warty olive-brown with dark spots and pale belly

entries.notes: The steppe's only true cold-weather amphibian; its spring chorus erupts from every pond after the thaw.

entries.name: Common spadefoot
behaviour: spade-like hind feet dig backward into loose sand to escape drought
explosive breeder after rain; giant tadpoles up to 17 cm long
lives buried for months between rains; appears only on humid nights

voxel_model.pattern: sandy with dark marbled blotches and vertical pupils

entries.notes: The desert's buried frog; it surfaces only in the wettest nights of a steppe summer, sometimes vanishing for years.

entries.name: Migratory locust
entries.migrates: swarms migrate hundreds of kilometres downwind
behaviour: solitary phase is gregarious phase waiting to happen after rain
swarms strip pasture entirely and march on fields
mechanically changes body colour and gregariousness with density

voxel_model.pattern: brown-green phase shifting to uniform swarming brown

entries.notes: The original locust; outbreak years turn the steppe into a moving, devouring ceiling.

entries.name: European praying mantis
behaviour: raptorial forelegs held 'in prayer' before striking
turns its triangular head to track prey with huge compound eyes
sexual cannibalism is real but rarer than legend

voxel_model.pattern: uniform green or brown; white spot in the foreleg armpit

entries.notes: An ambush predator the size of a finger; harmless to players and a favourite of anyone filming flower beds.

entries.name: Field cricket
behaviour: males chirp from burrow mouths with wings stridulating
fights rival males at burrow entrances with mandibles
its song is the measure of a hot afternoon on dry grass

voxel_model.pattern: glossy black with pale wing veins

entries.notes: The metronome of the steppe summer; its burrow-mouth chirping sets the tempo of a hot afternoon.

entries.name: Green tiger beetle
behaviour: one of the fastest insects relative to body length; sprints in zigzags
larvae wait in vertical burrow traps and snap prey passing the lip
metallic emerald with white elytral dots; loves bare sunny tracks

voxel_model.pattern: metallic green with six white spots

entries.notes: A jewelled sprinter of bare sandy paths; players who crouch to look at the ground will find one.

entries.name: Painted lady
behaviour: most widespread butterfly on Earth; migrates Africa to Europe and beyond
larvae eat thistles; adults commute along field margins
billions move in some years, streaming over deserts and seas

voxel_model.pattern: orange with black and white wing spots

entries.notes: The migration champion of butterflies; a fluttering tide can cross the steppe in spring and autumn.

entries.name: Wasp spider
behaviour: striped yellow-and-black abdomen mimics a wasp
zigzag 'stabilimentum' band decorates its orb web
males are dwarfs a quarter the female's size

voxel_model.pattern: wasp-striped abdomen with white stabilimentum in web

entries.notes: The zigzag-web spider of late-summer grassland; a striking and harmless ambusher among the seed heads.

entries.name: Lesser Asian scorpion
behaviour: hides under stones and in wall cracks by day
gives live birth; young ride on the mother's back
venom is mild; sting feels like a wasp sting, rarely dangerous

voxel_model.pattern: yellow-brown with darker stripes on segments

entries.notes: The scorpion a desert traveller finds under every third stone; a minor hazard rather than a killer.
